attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (AlmaLinux 9) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, protecting it from the kernel OOM killer. Verified via a real OOM event triggered by an unprotected memory-hog service (default oom_score_adj=0): the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the memory hog (PID 1422, oom_score_adj:0) per dmesg, while inventory-api (PID 1316, oom_score_adj:-1000) was never touched and kept answering HTTP 200 on /health and /inventory throughout. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline, issued systemctl reboot, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified inventory-api auto-started (enabled, active, correct oom_score_adj=-1000) and served correct data again post-reboot.
